detail_policy: Physical subsystem diagrams; at most five tables and eight selected fields per table. Catalog is complete; connectors are selective. No ClickHouse PK/FK or logical cardinality claims.

logical_relationships.label: Nullable source_check_run_id -> check_run_id; schema alerts may have no DQ check
table_name and optional dt identify the observed dataset/date; not a row FK
target_table and partition_dt describe run scope, not relational identity
snapshot_id correlates findings to observations; not enforced
qualified_name is a dataset identity convention; metadata is independently versioned
alert_key links incident audit evidence; blank/null context is allowed
Shared parent_run_id / incident identity; temporary events and durable memory differ
Legacy backfill request incident correlation; not a cross-store action-control FK
PostgreSQL incident authority projects a versioned ClickHouse snapshot through outbox
scope_json incident/date matching checks remediation blockers; no declared FK
alert_key associates a canonical public incident message with its alert
Guild/incident-scoped investigation identity and partial single-active uniqueness; no FK
Thread/guild metadata correlate Copilot claims with workspaces; no FK

groups.title: Warehouse / dbt derivation
groups.subtitle: Three physical ClickHouse relations. Derivation arrows are not foreign keys.
groups.caption: Selected partition, event identity and metric fields. dbt staging filters synthetic test rows and computes net amount; the mart aggregates by date/country/channel. ORDER BY does not enforce uniqueness.
notes: dbt: incremental insert_overwrite / MergeTree(). Bootstrap mart: ReplacingMergeTree(updated_at). See catalog caveat.

groups.title: Observability / checks and incidents
groups.subtitle: Analytical evidence and alert projection; logical links, never ClickHouse FKs.
groups.caption: Profiles and pipeline runs describe table/date scope. DQ alerts can refer to check_run_id; schema alerts need not. The open_alerts view is a filtered, non-FINAL read, not a transactional lifecycle authority.
notes: Link shown: alerts.source_check_run_id -> dq_check_results.check_run_id (nullable, logical only).

groups.title: Alerts / a filtered read is not authority
groups.subtitle: Two relations, one view derivation. The view does not collapse old alert versions.
groups.caption: open_alerts inherits all 20 alert columns, but only selected lifecycle fields are shown. Its literal filter includes open/triaged, not acknowledged. No FK, UNIQUE or FINAL is introduced by the view.
notes: WHERE status IN ('open', 'triaged') ORDER BY created_at DESC; source SQL does not use FINAL.

groups.title: Metadata / schema observations
groups.subtitle: Asset metadata and schema history share logical identity, not database constraints.
groups.caption: Findings correlate with schema observations through snapshot_id; qualified_name identifies the observed asset. Contract/version hashes preserve provenance. These ClickHouse fields are not FK/PK declarations.
notes: Logical labels: snapshot_id across the top; qualified_name between observation and asset registry.

groups.title: Triage / context and audit evidence
groups.subtitle: Temporary run context, durable incident memory and tool audit have different lifetimes.
groups.caption: parent_run_id and alert identity correlate context with memory. Temporary context uses an expires_at deletion TTL; incident memory remains durable. Audit is append evidence, not an approval or recovery engine.
notes: Context TTL: expires_at DELETE. Logical shared run/incident identity does not imply one-to-one records.

groups.title: Approvals / two distinct stores
groups.subtitle: Legacy backfill approval evidence and transactional action control coexist.
groups.caption: PostgreSQL is authoritative for current approval decisions and execution claims. ClickHouse retains history and receives projections, without a cross-store FK. Idempotent legacy import preserves available identifiers/history but does not grant pinned-source recovery eligibility.
notes: PostgreSQL has request PK + idempotency UNIQUE; ClickHouse ORDER BY request_id is not a UNIQUE constraint.

groups.title: Resolution / scoped revalidation
groups.subtitle: Only explicit PostgreSQL DDL references are solid FK connectors.
groups.caption: A revalidation request belongs to one incident control; an idempotency key points to a durable request. Child-to-parent FK references use NO ACTION. Fresh PASS does not automatically close an incident.
notes: N -> 1 required references, no cascading deletes. Revalidation DAG success can carry a blocked business result.

groups.title: Resolution / explicit closure decisions
groups.subtitle: Human-confirmed closure retains both incident and revalidation references.
groups.caption: The decision has two true FKs, one to the incident and one to its revalidation request. The diagram shows both. Application revision/scope/evidence gates add semantics that the FK constraints alone cannot enforce.
notes: Both decision FKs: ON DELETE NO ACTION / ON UPDATE NO ACTION. No autonomous or unconditional closure.

groups.title: Resolution / independent sink delivery
groups.subtitle: A committed incident decision is separate from projection, audit and Discord delivery.
groups.caption: incident_outbox references the incident control with one true FK. The unique event tuple prevents duplicate logical events. Projection/audit/delivery flags track separate sinks; there is no atomic cross-store transaction or blanket exactly-once guarantee.
notes: UNIQUE(alert_key, revision, event_type). Sink failures remain pending; successful closure is not delivery success.

groups.title: Discord / canonical workspaces
groups.subtitle: Composite identities and partial unique indexes; no declared Discord-table FKs.
groups.caption: Workspaces, event history and investigation claims correlate on guild/incident. Thread uniqueness is partial (nonempty thread IDs), and single-active investigation uniqueness applies only to claimed/uncertain rows. No field-level FK is invented.
notes: PK labels mark members of a composite key, not individual uniqueness. Full index predicates are in the catalog.

groups.title: Discord / claims and service identity
groups.subtitle: Durable request claims, user language preferences and bot-owned service messages.
groups.caption: These tables have independent PKs, not a declared relational parent-child chain. Copilot source_kind incorporates the command migration; service messages currently constrain kind to welcome. Physical BIGINT/TEXT identifier differences are preserved.
notes: Effective source_kind CHECK: message / modal / command. Preference CHECK: en / id. No conversation bodies copied here.

groups.title: Discord / incident delivery projection
groups.subtitle: ClickHouse message identity is a versioned projection, not transactional control.
groups.caption: The message registry correlates to alerts through alert_key. transport/author_id are included after the idempotent bot-delivery ALTERs; legacy_webhook remains a historical default, not an active architecture recommendation.
notes: ORDER BY alert_key is not a UNIQUE constraint. Historical webhook values do not imply supported webhook delivery.

groups.title: Recovery / pinned sources and publication
groups.subtitle: Versioned source facts, approved recovery state, and guarded partition publication.
groups.caption: Only PostgreSQL-declared foreign keys are shown. Recovery plans reference incident and approval records; executions reference plans; publication rows reference the dataset/partition revision; legacy approval projection rows reference approval requests. Snapshots and recovery outbox events have no declared FK.
notes: Other FKs: recovery_plans -> incident_controls + approval_requests; legacy import/projection -> approval_requests.
Those referenced tables are omitted from this 8-entity view. Publication FK is the tuple (dataset, partition_dt).
Source hashes bind content; they do not prove freshness or business validity.
